text.tspan: another computer; nothing realtime runs there
needs libnml — in practice another Linux with LinuxCNC
a GUI-only control PC; task, motion and HAL stay here
AXIS there needs AXIS_NO_HAL=1 — HAL is local memory —
and loses jog pins, pyvcp panels, classicladder
config: client.nml on it · server.nml on the machine

tspan.tspan: no authentication on TCP 5005 — anything that reaches it writes
client.nml / server.nml are NOT INSTALLED — source tree only
and declare emcStatus at 10240 B against 20480 — NML halves it again
unverified — run tool_watch to settle it

text.tspan: ordinary scheduling
SCHED_FIFO · rtapi_app
streamer / sampler — the same kind of memory, optional
RTAPI segments of their own, created in realtime and
attached by halstreamer / halsampler, ordinary processes
— so they cross this band too
keys 0x48535430+n (into HAL) · 0x48534130+n (out of HAL), 8 each
loaded, they are addf'd into a thread and run in the cycle
shipped configs: streamer 0 of 332 · sampler 1 (the panelui demo)
a scheduling boundary, not a kernel boundary
kernel modules only on the RTAI-
flavour — 1 of the 5 RTAPI flavours;
uspace/RTAI is user space too

write —

loaded by loadrt like motmod — rtapi_app_main()
their functs are addf'd into whichever thread the integrator picks
23 driver files · hostmot2 alone: 42 modules, one driver
every driver is a HAL component — its pins live in HAL memory

tspan.tspan: ①②③④⑤ is one shipped CONVENTION, not a rule.

text.tspan: Of the 55 shipped configs that addf both a hardware read and motion-command-handler,
— and one does not:
configs/by_interface/general_mechatronics/GM6-PCI/3-axis-servo.hal reads its board
the controller has run. Reorder the addf lines and you reorder the machine's cycle.

text.tspan: — a container, or a subdivision of its parent

tspan.tspan: Why it is coloured this way:

text.tspan: so the colour can be checked, not admired.
• every GREEN box must sit inside rtapi_app
• every GREY box must sit above the remote line
• the ORANGE box must sit below the machine line
• every WHITE box must carry at least one link
All four hold as drawn.
: "process" and "non-realtime" are not the
same thing — rtapi_app is a process and it lives below the line.
The letters on the NML strip say what each side DOES: the file declares task RW on
emcCommand, a permission it never uses.
